subject: Transportation Systems
title: Bridge Loads and Safety Factors
description: Learn Bridge Loads and Safety Factors in one minute.

hook.text: A bridge is designed to hold far more than it will ever carry. The extra capacity is the safety factor.

buildup.text: Engineers calculate dead load (the bridge's own weight), live load (traffic), and environmental loads (wind, ice).

discovery.text: A typical safety factor of 2.0 means the bridge can handle twice its expected maximum load before failure.

twist.text: Bridges don't usually fail from overload. Corrosion, fatigue cracks, and poor maintenance are the real killers.

climax.text: The 2018 Genoa bridge collapse killed 43 people. Corroded tendons—known about for years—went unrepaired.

punchline.text: Bridges aren't built to last. They're maintained to last.

quiz.question: What does a safety factor of 2.0 mean for a bridge?
options: It can handle twice its expected maximum load
